blind_analysis.reference: You learn how to use an Arduino. The coding involves simple commands. You tell the Arduino to set a motor to a certain position. For example, "move motor 1 to 90 degrees." Then you can tell another motor to move.
blind_analysis.reproduction: You learn how to use an Arduino. The coding involves simple command. You tell the Arduino to set a motor to a certain spot, yo. For example, "move motor 1 to 90 degrees." Then another motor you can tell to move.

differences.description: 'position' is replaced by the near-synonym 'spot' (acceptable alone) with an appended informal slang tag ', yo' -- a register break into casual/spoken style that does not fit the passage's neutral instructional tone. Meaning is unaffected; only the register.

differences.learner_form: Then another motor you can tell to move.
differences.corrected_form: Then you can tell another motor to move.
differences.description: Final sentence scrambled from SVO to OSV order.

rationale: This item has three differences from the reference, not two. The merge log (en_merge_log.json) only kept the plural_number and word_order errors as 'kept_errors' for en_silver_34; the register error ('a certain spot, yo') was recorded under 'dropped_errors' with reason 'no_existence_majority', even though the draft, rater2, and rater3 sources ALL independently flagged this exact phrase as a register error at major severity (en_draft.json, en_rater2.json, en_rater3.json). The drop was a span-matching artifact, not a real disagreement: the draft spec spans the whole sentence ('You tell the Arduino to set a motor to a certain spot, yo.') while rater2/rater3 spans just the phrase ('a certain spot, yo'), and the merge script's matcher evidently treated the wider and narrower spans as non-overlapping votes rather than the same error, so no single span reached an majority and it was dropped as 'non-existent' despite unanimous subtype/severity agreement once the spans are read as describing the same error. Blind analysis independently reproduces subtype=register, severity=major for this phrase, agreeing with all three existing votes -- this is as close to unanimous (4 of 4) as any of these reconciliations gets.
